senses.en: fair; just (a rule, a split, a decision)
fair to people; impartial: 对 + person + 公平

examples.zh: 他什么都不做，这不公平！
examples.en: He doesn't do a thing. That's not fair!
examples.analysis: 公平 is the predicate: 这 'this' + 不公平 'is not fair'. Like most adjectives, it needs no 是 before it. 什么都不做 'does nothing at all': 什么 + 都 + a negative means 'not anything'. 不公平 is the everyday complaint 'unfair'.

examples.zh: 我们经理对大家都很公平。
examples.en: Our manager is fair to everyone.
examples.analysis: 对 + person + 公平 says 'fair to someone': 对大家 'toward everyone' comes before the adjective. 都 sums up 大家, 'all of them'. In a plain statement like this, unstressed 很 mostly links the adjective; stressed, it means 'very'.

examples.en: Half each. That's the fairest way.
examples.analysis: 最 + 公平 makes the superlative, 'fairest'. 这样 'this way' is the subject and points back to the plan. 一人一半 'one person, one half' is a common way to propose splitting something, such as a bill or a dish.

related.en: the same; 大家都一样 'it's the same for everyone'

senses.en: shoe; shoes (any footwear)

measure.note: 一双鞋 a pair of shoes; 只 (zhī) for one shoe of a pair

examples.en: How much are these shoes?
examples.analysis: 鞋 is the topic of the question. In casual shop talk people often say 这鞋 with no measure word; the full form is 这双鞋 'this pair of shoes'. 多少钱 'how much money' is the standard price question and goes at the end.

examples.en: Come on in. You don't need to take your shoes off.
examples.analysis: 换鞋 'change shoes' means taking off outdoor shoes and putting on slippers at the door, a common custom in Chinese homes. 不用 + verb means 'there's no need to'. 吧 turns 进来 into a friendly invitation.

examples.zh: 我的鞋有点儿小，穿着不舒服。
examples.en: My shoes are a bit small. They're uncomfortable.
examples.analysis: 鞋 has no plural form; 'shoe' or 'shoes' comes from context. 有点儿 + adjective 'a bit', usually for something unwelcome. 穿着 'when worn': verb + 着 sets the situation, and 不舒服 'not comfortable' gives the result. 穿 is the verb for shoes.

collocations.en: to change shoes (at home: into slippers at the door)
to put on or wear shoes

related.en: to wear; the verb for shoes and clothes

meaning: to take out, collect, pick up (money, tickets, medicine)

senses.en: to withdraw; to take out (money): 取钱
to collect; to pick up something kept for you (tickets, a parcel, medicine)

examples.en: I'm going to the bank to take out some cash.
examples.analysis: 取钱 is the set phrase for 'withdraw money'. The pattern 去 + place + verb gives the purpose: 'go to the bank (to) withdraw money'. No word for 'to' is needed; the order shows it.

examples.en: Have you picked up the tickets?
examples.analysis: 取票 means collecting tickets already booked, for example from a station machine or a cinema counter. 了 marks the action as done, and 吗 turns the statement into a yes/no question.

examples.en: Could you go and pick up my medicine for me?
examples.analysis: 取药 is collecting medicine from a pharmacy, often the hospital pharmacy after a doctor's prescription. 帮我 + verb 'do something for me'; 你能…吗 'can you…?' makes it a polite request.

related.en: to take; to carry; the general word, often used instead of 取 in casual speech
to deposit (存钱 put money in the bank)

senses.en: short in length (hair, clothes, a road)
short in time; brief

examples.zh: 这件衣服有点儿短，有长一点儿的吗？
examples.en: This is a bit short. Do you have a longer one?
examples.analysis: 短 is the predicate after 有点儿 'a bit (too)'. Its opposite 长 then appears in 长一点儿的 'a slightly longer one': adjective + 一点儿 compares, and 的 turns the phrase into 'one'.

examples.en: There wasn't enough time. I didn't get to finish.
examples.analysis: 短 also covers time: 时间太短了 'the time was too short'. 太 + adjective + 了 is the usual 'too …' frame. 没说完 'didn't finish saying': 完 after the verb marks completion, and 没 says it didn't happen.

examples.en: How come your hair is so short now?
examples.analysis: 怎么 here asks 'how come', with surprise, not 'in what way'. 这么 + 短 'this short'. 了 at the end marks a change: the hair was longer before. 你头发 drops 的, which is common with body parts in speech.

related.en: short in height (a person); 短 is not used for people's height

senses.en: the Earth (the planet we live on)

examples.en: The Earth is getting hotter and hotter.
examples.analysis: 地球 is the subject. 越来越 + adjective says 'more and more …', and 了 at the end marks the change as happening now. People say 地球越来越热 when talking about global warming; for plain summer heat they say 天气越来越热.

examples.en: Do you know how big the Earth is?
examples.analysis: 地球有多大 'how big the Earth is' is the object of 你知道…吗 'do you know…?'. 有 + 多 + adjective asks about degree: 有多大 'how big', 有多远 'how far'. A typical question between a parent and a child.

examples.zh: 我看过地球的照片，真漂亮。
examples.en: I've seen photos of the Earth. So beautiful.
examples.analysis: 地球的照片 'photos of the Earth': 地球 + 的 describes the noun after it. 看过 'have seen' uses 过 for past experience. 真漂亮 has no subject; from context it means the photos (or the Earth in them) look beautiful.

meaning: to pass by or through (a place); what happened (the course of events)

senses.en: to pass by; to go through or via (a place)
what happened; the course of events: 事情的经过
to go through; to undergo (a period, a process): 经过一年

examples.zh: 去公司要经过一个公园。
examples.en: On the way to the office you pass a park.
examples.analysis: 经过 takes the place as its object: 经过一个公园 'pass a park'. 要 here means 'you have to, it involves'. 去公司 'going to the office' sets the frame, so the sentence describes the route.

examples.en: Does this bus go past the hospital?
examples.analysis: 经过 + place asks about a route: does it go past or through there? 这车 is casual for 这辆车, with the measure word 辆 (liàng) dropped; 车 covers buses as well as cars. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

examples.zh: 你能告诉我事情的经过吗？
examples.en: Can you tell me how it all happened?
examples.analysis: Here 经过 is a noun: 事情的经过 'the course of the matter', the events from start to finish. It is the object of 告诉我 'tell me'. A doctor, a police officer or a worried friend might ask this.

related.en: through; by means of; to pass (an exam); for passing by a place, 经过 is the usual word
to pass by on the way somewhere else: 我路过你家

senses.en: phone or network signal; reception
a signal; a sign given to someone

examples.en: There's no signal here.
examples.analysis: 没有 + noun 'there isn't any …', with the place 这里 as the topic in front. In daily talk 信号 usually means phone or Wi-Fi reception; 没信号 is the shorter spoken form.

examples.en: Is the signal bad where you are?
examples.analysis: 你那边 'your side, where you are' is the usual phrase on a call. 信号 + 好 / 不好 is the everyday way to rate reception; 信号很差 'the signal is bad' is also common. 吗 turns it into a yes/no question.

examples.zh: 地铁里信号不太好，我出去再给你打。
examples.en: The signal's not great in the subway. I'll call you back when I'm out.
examples.analysis: 信号不太好 'not very good': 不太 softens the complaint. 再 here means 'then, after that', not 'again': first get out, then call. 打 alone is short for 打电话 'make a call' when the context is clear.

senses.en: weekend; Saturday and Sunday

measure.note: 这个周末 this weekend; 上个周末 last weekend

examples.en: What are your plans for the weekend?
examples.analysis: 周末 comes first as a time word; Chinese puts 'when' before the verb, at the start or right after the subject. 打算 is a noun here, 'plan'. 有什么打算 'what plans do you have' is a standard small-talk question.

examples.en: I have to work this weekend.
examples.analysis: 这个周末 'this weekend': 这 + measure word 个 + 周末. 得 is read děi here and means 'have to'. 上班 'go to work' is the everyday verb for a working day.

examples.en: Let's go hiking together this weekend!
examples.analysis: No subject is needed; 吧 at the end makes the line a suggestion, 'let's'. 周末 sets the time, then 一起 'together' + 去 + activity. 爬山, literally 'climb a mountain', is the usual word for hiking up hills.

related.en: to rest; to have time off

meaning: to push; to put off (a meeting, a date)

senses.en: to push (a door, a cart, a bike)
to put off; to push back (推到 + time)

examples.zh: 这个门是推的，你别拉了。
examples.en: It's a push door. Stop pulling it.
examples.analysis: 是…的 describes the door's type: 是推的 'is a push one'. 推 'push' and 拉 'pull' are the pair printed on doors. 别 + verb + 了 means 'stop doing it', said to someone already pulling.

examples.zh: 自行车坏了，我推回家了。
examples.en: My bike broke, so I pushed it home.
examples.analysis: 推 + 回家 'push (it) back home': what follows the verb says where the push went. The bike is not repeated as an object; Chinese drops it once it is clear. Each 了 marks a completed event.

examples.zh: 明天的会能不能推到下午？
examples.en: Could tomorrow's meeting be pushed back to the afternoon?
examples.analysis: Here 推 means 'put off': 推到 + time 'push back to'. 明天的会 'tomorrow's meeting' is the topic, with no passive marker needed. 能不能 'can or can't' is a soft way to ask for a change.

collocations.en: to push a cart or bike

senses.en: to be used to; to get used to (习惯 + noun or verb phrase)
habit; custom

measure.note: 一个好习惯; 是个坏习惯

examples.zh: 你习惯这里的生活了吗？
examples.en: Are you used to life here yet?
examples.analysis: 习惯 is a verb here: 习惯 + 这里的生活 'be used to life here'. 了 marks a change of state, so 习惯…了吗 asks 'have you become used to it yet?'. People often ask newcomers this.

examples.zh: 我还不习惯这么早起床。
examples.en: I'm still not used to getting up this early.
examples.analysis: 习惯 can take a whole verb phrase: 习惯 + 这么早起床 'getting up this early'. 还不 'still not' says the change hasn't happened yet. 这么 + 早 'this early' comes before the verb 起床.

examples.zh: 睡觉前看手机是个坏习惯。
examples.en: Looking at your phone before bed is a bad habit.
examples.analysis: Here 习惯 is a noun with 坏 'bad' before it. 是个 is short for 是一个 'is a'. The whole action 睡觉前看手机 'looking at the phone before sleeping' is the subject; 前 after a verb means 'before'.

meaning: more and more; increasingly (越来越 + adjective)

senses.en: more and more; increasingly (before an adjective, or a verb like 喜欢, 像, 会, 习惯)

examples.en: It's getting colder and colder.
examples.analysis: 越来越 goes right before the adjective: 越来越冷 'colder and colder'. 了 at the end marks the change. 越来越 already gives the degree, so 很 is not added: 越来越很冷 is wrong.

examples.zh: 你的中文说得越来越好了！
examples.en: Your Chinese is getting better and better!
examples.analysis: Here 越来越好 comes after 说得, the frame that rates how an action is done: verb + 得 + comment. So the sentence says the speaking keeps improving. A friendly compliment learners often hear.

examples.zh: 我觉得他越来越像他爸爸了。
examples.en: I think he looks more and more like his dad.
examples.analysis: 越来越 also works before some verbs of feeling or likeness, such as 像 'resemble' or 喜欢 'like'. 他越来越像他爸爸 is typically said of a growing child. 我觉得 'I think' frames it as an opinion.

related.en: 越…越… the more … the more …: 越快越好

senses.en: a list of names (guests, people taking part, staff)

measure.note: 一份名单 a list; 张 (zhāng) for a list on a single sheet

examples.en: Am I on the list?
examples.analysis: 名单上 'on the list': a list is treated like a surface, so Chinese adds 上 after it. Then 有我 'there is me'. Chinese uses 有 'there is' here, where English uses 'am … on'.

examples.zh: 你的名字我写在名单上了。
examples.en: I've put your name on the list.
examples.analysis: 你的名字 is moved to the front as the topic: 'your name, I've written it…'. 写在 + place 'write on', so 写在名单上 'written on the list'. 了 marks it as done.

examples.en: Who has the list?
examples.analysis: Chinese says where the list is: 在 + person + 那儿 'with someone'. A person after 在 normally needs 那儿 or 这儿 to become a place. 名单 is the subject at the front.

senses.en: park; public garden

measure.note: 一个公园; 座 (zuò) sounds more written, for a large park: 一座公园

examples.zh: 吃完饭我们去公园走走吧。
examples.en: Let's go for a walk in the park after dinner.
examples.analysis: 去公园 + 走走 'go to the park and walk a bit': going somewhere and the purpose are just two verbs in a row. Doubling the verb, 走走, makes it short and relaxed. 吃完饭 'after eating' sets the time; 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.en: There's a park next to my place.
examples.analysis: Place + 有 + thing is how Chinese says 'there is … somewhere': 我家旁边 'next to my home' comes first, then 有个公园. 有个 is the spoken short form of 有一个.

examples.en: Is the park crowded on weekends?
examples.analysis: 公园里 'in the park': 里 'inside' follows the place noun. 人多吗 'are there many people?', literally 'are people many?', asks if it is crowded; Chinese makes 多 the predicate.

related.en: garden, often attached to a home or building

senses.en: bird

measure.note: 一只鸟; 群 (qún) for a flock: 一群鸟

examples.en: Look, there's a bird in the tree!
examples.analysis: 树上有只鸟 is place + 有 + thing. 只 is the measure word for birds and many other animals, such as cats and dogs, and 一 is often dropped in speech: 有只 = 有一只. Chinese says 'on' the tree (上) where English says 'in'.

examples.zh: 那是什么鸟？叫得真好听。
examples.en: What bird is that? It sings so beautifully.
examples.analysis: 什么 + 鸟 'what kind of bird'. 叫 is the verb for animal sounds, birdsong included. 叫得真好听 'sings really nicely' uses verb + 得 + comment to rate the sound.

examples.en: My grandpa loves keeping birds.
examples.analysis: 养鸟 'keep birds (as pets)': 养 means to raise or keep an animal. It is a traditional hobby of many older men, especially in cities such as Beijing. 很喜欢 + verb phrase 'really like doing'.

senses.en: healthy (a person, food, a habit)
health

examples.zh: 我奶奶八十了，身体还很健康。
examples.en: My grandma is eighty and still in good health.
examples.analysis: 身体健康 'the body is healthy' is a natural way to say someone is in good health (in casual talk 身体很好 is just as common); 健康 is the adjective predicate. 还 'still' adds 'even at this age'. 八十了 'is eighty now' uses the number as a predicate, with 了 for the age reached.

examples.zh: 别喝那么多酒，对健康不好。
examples.en: Don't drink so much. It's bad for your health.
examples.analysis: Here 健康 is a noun, 'health'. 对 + 健康 + 不好 'bad for health' is the standard frame; 对身体不好 'bad for the body' means the same and is just as common. 别 + verb is a direct 'don't'.

examples.en: Is skipping dinner healthy?
examples.analysis: The first part, 不吃晚饭 'not eating dinner', is the topic; then 健康吗 asks 'is that healthy?'. As an adjective, 健康 describes habits and food as well as people.

collocations.en: in good health (also a common wish)

related.en: body; health: 身体好 'in good health'

meaning: not enough; not … enough (不够 + adjective)

senses.en: to be not enough; to fall short
not … enough (不够 + adjective): 不够大

examples.en: There isn't enough food. Let's order two more dishes.
examples.analysis: 不够 is the predicate: 菜不够 'the dishes are not enough'. 再 + verb 'some more', 点 'order (food)', and 两个 leaves out 菜 because it is clear. 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.zh: 我的钱不够，你能借我一点儿吗？
examples.en: I don't have enough money. Could you lend me some?
examples.analysis: Owner + thing + 不够 is the usual way to say 'I don't have enough …': 我的钱不够. 借 + person + amount 'lend someone some'; 一点儿 'a little' keeps the request modest.

examples.en: This room isn't big enough.
examples.analysis: Here 不够 works like an adverb before an adjective: 不够大 'not big enough'. The order is the reverse of English: 不够 first, then the adjective. Same pattern: 不够快 'not fast enough', 不够好 'not good enough'.

related.en: few; little: a small amount, not necessarily less than needed: 钱少 'not much money' vs 钱不够 'not enough'

senses.en: direction; which way
direction in life or work; aim

measure.note: 这个方向; 哪个方向

examples.en: We've gone the wrong way.
examples.analysis: 走错方向 'walked in the wrong direction': 错 after the verb says the result was wrong, and 方向 is the object. 了 at the end marks the new situation the speaker has just noticed.

examples.en: Which way is the hospital?
examples.analysis: 在 + 哪个方向 'in which direction' asks for the general direction, not step-by-step directions. 哪个 'which' is 哪 + measure word 个. 方向 is one way to say 'which way'; 医院在哪边？ is another common one.

examples.zh: 你往这个方向走，十分钟就到了。
examples.en: Head this way and you'll be there in ten minutes.
examples.analysis: 往 + direction + 走 'go toward': 往这个方向走 'walk this way'. 十分钟就到了 'ten minutes and you're there': 就 stresses that it is soon, and 了 marks the arrival as the result.

meaning: to carry on (doing); then, next; catch!

senses.en: to carry on; to continue (接着 + verb)
then; next; right after that
to catch (something thrown): 接着！

examples.en: Don't stop. Go on.
examples.analysis: 接着 + verb means 'carry on doing': 接着说 'keep talking, go on'. It is said when someone pauses or gets interrupted. 别停 'don't stop' is a direct command with 别.

examples.zh: 他先去了银行，接着又去了医院。
examples.en: He went to the bank first, and then to the hospital.
examples.analysis: Here 接着 is an adverb, 'then, right after that', linking two events. 先 'first' sets up the order, and 又 adds the second trip. 先…接着… is a common way to tell a sequence.

examples.en: Here you go. Catch!
examples.analysis: Said when tossing something to someone. 接 means 'catch, receive', and 着 in a command adds 'take it and hold on', as in 拿着 'hold this'. 给你 'here you go' warns that something is coming your way.

related.en: then; afterwards; less tied to right after

senses.en: senior high school (in China, the three years after junior high)

measure.note: 一所高中; 个 (gè) in casual speech

examples.en: We were classmates in high school.
examples.analysis: 高中 describes 同学 directly, with no 的: 高中同学 'high-school classmates'. 是 carries no tense, so this is the normal way to say it even years later, where English says 'were'.

examples.en: Is your daughter in high school yet?
examples.analysis: 上 + school 'attend': 上高中 'be in high school', 上大学 'go to university'. 了 marks a change, so with 吗 it asks whether she has reached that stage yet.

examples.zh: 高中的时候我不太喜欢学习。
examples.en: In high school I didn't much like studying.
examples.analysis: 高中的时候 'in my high-school days': noun + 的时候 marks a period and comes first. 不太喜欢 'don't much like' is softer than 不喜欢. The past comes from context; the verb does not change.

meaning: just right; just in time; to happen to

senses.en: just right (size, amount, timing)
as it happens; happen to (a lucky overlap)
exactly; just (an amount or time): 正好一百块, 正好十点

examples.zh: 这件衣服不大不小，正好。
examples.en: This one is not too big and not too small. Just right.
examples.analysis: Here 正好 is an adjective, 'just right'. 不大不小 'neither too big nor too small' follows a common pattern: 不 + adjective + 不 + its opposite. 正好 then gives the verdict, often said alone when trying something on.

examples.en: You came at just the right time. The food's just ready.
examples.analysis: 来得正好 'came at just the right moment' uses verb + 得 + comment, with 正好 rating the timing. 刚做好 'has just been made': 刚 'just now' + 做, with 好 after the verb meaning 'done, ready'.

examples.zh: 我正好要去超市，帮你买吧。
examples.en: As it happens, I'm going to the supermarket. I'll get it for you.
examples.analysis: Here 正好 is an adverb before the verb, 'as it happens'. It marks a lucky overlap: I'm going anyway, so helping costs nothing. 帮你买 'buy it for you'; 吧 makes the offer casual.

collocations.en: not too big, not too small: just right

related.en: just right; happen to (the same two uses)
